record.title: Miller–Vissuet's MSTD–MDTS conjecture for dihedral groups
record.literal_statement:
Let $n\geq 3$ be an integer, and let

$$
D_{2n}:=\langle r,s:r^n=s^2=1,\ r^{-1}s=sr\rangle
$$

be the dihedral group of order $2n$. An MSTD subset is a subset with more distinct pairwise sums than distinct pairwise differences, while an MDTS subset has more distinct pairwise differences than distinct pairwise sums. **Miller–Vissuet's conjecture.** There are more MSTD subsets of $D_{2n}$ than MDTS subsets of $D_{2n}$. This conjecture concerns the prevalence of sum-dominant and difference-dominant subsets in finite non-abelian groups and was proposed on the basis of theoretical and computational evidence; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for cyclically 4-connected cubic flow roots
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cyclically 4-connected cubic graph, and let $F(G,t)$ denote its flow polynomial. Let $\tau=(1+\sqrt{5})/2$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many cyclically 4-connected cubic graphs have a flow root in

$$
(2,\tau^2-\epsilon).
$$

This is the flow-polynomial counterpart of the finiteness conjecture for 4-connected plane triangulations. The source presents it as open.
record.source_name: Bill Jackson, “Zeros of Chromatic and Flow Polynomials of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0205047 (2002).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0205047

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2002). “Indeed it is an open problem to determine the supremum of the real chromatic roots of plane triangulations.”

record.title: Conjecture on flow roots of 3-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 3-connected graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $F(G,t)$ denote its flow polynomial. Let $\phi\approx1.749$ be the flow root of $K_5$ in $(1,2)$. **3-connected flow-root conjecture.**

$$
F(G,t)\text{ is non-zero with sign }(-1)^{m-n}\quad\text{for }t\in(1,\phi).
$$

If $G$ is not an Eulerian graph with $m-n$ odd, the same conclusion should hold for $t\in(1,2)$. This is the flow-polynomial analogue of the preceding conjecture for 3-connected chromatic graphs; the source gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Bill Jackson, “Zeros of Chromatic and Flow Polynomials of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0205047 (2002).

record.title: Packing version of Dinitz's problem
record.literal_statement:
For an integer $n\geq 3$, let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_n\mathbin\square K_n$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\chi_\ell^\star$ denote the list packing number.

**Packing version of Dinitz's problem.** For $n\geq 3$,

$$
\chi_\ell^\star(K_n\mathbin\square K_n)=n+1.
$$

The graph $K_n\mathbin\square K_n$ is the line graph of $K_{n,n}$, and its ordinary list chromatic number is $n$ by Galvin's theorem, whereas the paper shows that its list packing number exceeds $n$. Determining whether the exact value is $n+1$ remains open.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Ewan Davies and Ross J. Kang, “List packing number of bounded degree graphs”, arXiv:2303.01246 (2023).

record.title: Minimality conjecture for the constructed bicommutative system
record.literal_statement: Let $n=4k+7$, $m=2k+3$, and $k\geq 2$. Let $\mathcal{A}_m$ be the constructed $m$-bicommutative system in $\mathcal{P}_n(m)$. **Bicommutative-system minimality conjecture.** Does $\mathcal{A}_m$ have minimum size among all $m$-bicommutative systems in $\mathcal{P}_n(m)$? The question concerns whether the explicit construction is optimal for these finite parameters; no resolution is supplied in the source.

record.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a loopless 3-connected graph with $n$ vertices, and let $P(G,t)$ be its chromatic polynomial. Let $\alpha\approx 1.781$ be the chromatic root of $K_{3,4}$ in $(1,2)$. **Thomassen's conjecture.**

$$
P(G,t)\text{ is non-zero with sign }(-1)^n\quad\text{for }t\in(1,\alpha).
$$

If $G$ is not a bipartite graph with an odd number of vertices, the same conclusion should hold throughout $(1,2)$. The second assertion is described as a slight strengthening of a conjecture previously given in the cited source; the proof method is obstructed by edge deletion and contraction producing graphs of connectivity two.

literal.statement:
Let $G$ be a loopless planar graph, and let $P(G,t)$ be its chromatic polynomial. **Thomassen's conjecture.** The real chromatic roots of planar graphs are dense everywhere in

$$
\left[\frac{32}{27},4\right].
$$

Real chromatic roots are already known to be dense in $[32/27,3]$. Extending density to $4$ would show that planar graphs have real chromatic roots arbitrarily close to the four-colour threshold.
